item.description: The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage reached 6.66% on average Thursday.

item.title: Are you choosing to stay single? We want to hear from you
item.description: Solo living, solo travel, and solo dining are all being embraced as more adults are choosing to remain single. Many Americans aren't interested in dating, and being single is a symbol of autonomy.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: European soccer leaders to boycott the World Cup in an unprecedented step
item.description: European soccer associations said they would boycott the World Cup unless FIFA reverses a controversial deal to sell minority stakes to the marquee soccer tournament.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The economy slowed a bit -- but Americans continued to spend
item.description: The U.S. economy grew at an annual rate of 1.5% in the spring, according to the Commerce Department. That's a modest slowdown from the previous quarter — but consumer spending picked up steam.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. economy grew at an annual rate of 1.5% in the spring, according to the Commerce Department. That's a modest slowdown from the previous quarter — but consumer spending picked up steam.

(Image credit: Joe Raedle)

item.title: The renter-owner wealth gap is wider than ever, as many are priced out of buying
item.description: Housing has long been the largest source of wealth for middle income families. But many renters cannot afford to buy as housing prices soar, which could fuel a generational divide.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: A divided Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady despite high inflation
item.description: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged Wednesday. Fed policymakers say they remain committed to curbing stubborn inflation.

item.title: More Americans are going bankrupt. What does that mean?
item.description: The bankruptcy rate has risen about 48% between 2022 and 2025, although it's still below pre-pandemic levels.

item.title: FIFA has a new plan to raise billions of dollars: Selling stakes in the World Cup
item.description: FIFA has a complex plan to sell chunks of its commercial rights to the World Cup to minority investors, including a firm run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Jared Kushner.

item.title: As many are priced out of buying, the renter-owner wealth gap is wider than ever
item.description: Record high housing costs have pushed the wealth gap between renters and owners wider than ever. It's been a boon for owners even as many others are priced out.

item.title: AI tokens could become the kilowatt-hour of the AI age
item.description: AI companies use tokens to track usage and bill customers. Now economists are using them to track the spread of AI through the economy.
